concepts.label: Key-Value Data Operations (get/upsert/insert/replace/remove) via the Collection API
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the Key-Value API is explicitly positioned in this page as an ALTERNATIVE to SQL++ for single-document operations ('we very strongly recommend using the key-value API for this instead [of SQL++]'), so it is a genuinely different access path, not a wrapper around any n1ql:* statement. No reuse candidate applies.

concepts.label: Durability Options (Majority, MajorityAndPersistToActive, PersistToMajority, client-verified durability)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - client-library option wrapping a server durability feature, but the durability *levels* themselves are a server-side concept (Durable Writes) that this page just exposes as an SDK option enum

concepts.label: KV Range Scan (rangeScan, prefixScan, samplingScan)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - explicitly framed as an alternative to a SQL++ query with a primary index, for a different concurrency/latency tradeoff, not as a wrapper around any n1ql:* statement.

relations.subject: sdk:kv-operations
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused predicate, directionality is KV preferred over SQL++ for single-doc ops (inverse of the usual DDL mustUseInsteadWhen direction)
relations.evidence: SQL++ (formerly N1QL) can also be used to perform many single-document operations but we very strongly recommend using the key-value API for this instead, as it can be much more efficient.

relations.subject: sdk:kv-range-scan
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - opposite direction this time: SQL++ recommended over KV range scan for high-concurrency/low-latency needs
relations.evidence: If your application does many scans at once, or requires low latency results, we recommend using SQL++ (with a primary index on the collection) instead of KV range scan.

relations.subject: sdk:kv-range-scan
relations.evidence: A range scan gives you documents from a collection, even if you don't know the document IDs. This feature requires Couchbase Server 7.6 or newer.

relations.subject: sdk:durability
relations.evidence: If a version of Couchbase Server lower than 6.5 is being used then the application can fall-back to 'client verified' durability. Here the SDK will do a simple poll of the replicas and only return once the requested durability level is achieved.

relations.subject: sdk:document-expiration
relations.evidence: If you are using Couchbase Server 7.0 or later, set the `preserveExpiry` option when updating the document ... Prior to Couchbase 7.0, it's necessary to fetch the previous expiry and set it again.

relations.subject: sdk:kv-operations
relations.evidence: Our [Query Engine](sqlpp-queries-with-sdk.md) enables retrieval of information using the SQL-like syntax of SQL++.

cross_product_finding: This page makes the strongest explicit case in the batch for the Key-Value API being a genuinely DIFFERENT kind of thing from SQL++, not merely an alternate way to invoke it: the page itself states SQL++ COULD be used for single-document CRUD but the KV API is recommended instead for performance reasons ('no query parsing overhead ... highly optimized memcached binary protocol'). This is the opposite relationship from provisioning-cluster-resources.json (where the SDK method IS the statement) - here the SDK method is presented as an alternative, competing access path to the SAME data, not a wrapper over any SQL++ statement at all. KV Range Scan repeats this pattern in the opposite direction (SQL++ is recommended over it for certain workloads). I therefore minted sdk:kv-operations and sdk:kv-range-scan rather than reusing any n1ql:* concept, and captured the competing relationship explicitly via mustUseInsteadWhen in both directions rather than picking one 'true' vocabulary.
